decisions.reason: After only one year on the market its value is still uncertain, and keeping a catalog display costs little, so the option stays open.
The pegboard display is a distinct variant whose prospects are still unresolved, and keeping it costs little.
The standard quarter-pallet display fits the core cardboard business, and early evidence gives no reason to abandon it, though it overlaps with Product A.
The eighth-pallet format widens the firm's range of display options at little cost, and the results so far are too early to judge.
The wooden pallet lies outside the core paper business, which makes it a likelier candidate to drop, but one year reveals too little to justify abandoning it yet.
Demand for media-product displays faces structural decline, which raises the drop risk, but its value has not yet clearly been shown to be unrealizable.
